By being well-prepared in the way that Avraham teaches us, we make the first move, and leave no room for the Yetzer Hara's attack!

Anticipating mitzvah opportunities - and planning ahead for them! - ensures that we’ll have whatever we need to do what Hashem wants.

The way we attack our enemy, the Yetzer Hara, is by putting positive and true thoughts into our heads. We tell our Yetzer

Hara that Hashem is the one who takes care of all our needs, and the best way to take care of myself is by ONLY doing what Hashem wants. Those thoughts grow into good feelings that will lead into even better actions.

Thinking like Avraham will create good feelings that can lead to even better actions.

Look at the following scene and identify: How could the Yetzer Tov help you to be prepared and strike first?
